newsitem.title: UK: UK natgas mixed, Aug and Sep up while Q4 stable.
newsitem.headline: UK natgas mixed, Aug and Sep up while Q4 stable.

text.p: The UK spot natural gas market saw mixed activity on Thursday as August and September rose while the fourth quarter remained stable.

"The main news is August and September coming up and Q4 staying stable," said one broker. August traded at 9.625 pence and 9.60 pence a therm, up from Wednesday's levels, while September also rose to trade at 9.80 pence. September was offered at 9.90 pence by the close, a broker said.

And Q4, which rose sharply on Wednesday, maintained most of its gains on Thursday. It traded twice at 13.10 pence a therm and was rumoured to have traded at 13.05 pence as well, although this was not confirmed. By the close the bid/offer spread was 13.05/13.15 pence, down by just 0.05 pence a therm from Wednesday.
October, which had traded several times on Tuesday between 10.80 pence and 10.90 pence, was active again on Thursday with four trades reported between 10.90 pence and 10.95 pence.

One trader said there was a good opportunity for buying October gas from buyers of Q4, who only really wanted gas in November and December and were happy to sell on the October element of the quarter.

A seller at St Fergus reported receiving some interest in the October gas year. But bids were at 12.35 pence and the seller was offering 12.60 pence. This gap was too wide to be bridged and no trade was concluded. The gas year was done at least twice at the NBP at 12.90 pence and closed in a slightly tighter range than on Wednesday, at 12.85/12.95 pence a therm.

IPE futures enjoyed another busy day, with 290 lots done. It has now traded actively every day this week, and a number of players on the OTC market were encouraged to see IPE volumes picking up after a long period of only sporadic trade.
IPE price movements were mixed, as they were on the OTC market, with August and September up while January and February, which have risen recently, both slipped.
